subject: number of groups in dataframe influence p-value of pairwise comparison

messages.author: 82f4cbd8cffc3818
messages.subject: number of groups in dataframe influence p-value of pairwise comparison
parts:
Dear MSstats Team

We've recently observed that the p-value calculated by the groupComparison function of MSstats sometimes is (strongly!) affected by other groups in the same dataframe - even when these other groups are not used. Hence the outcome of the comparison of Group "A vs B" is different if we use a dataProcess dataframe with Groups:

A, B, C, D, E (but only make comparison A vs B)
=>  Q9Z1D1 (pValue: 0.15232117, DF: 25)

vs. 

A, B (and also only compare A vs B)
=>  Q9Z1D1 (pValue: 0.00000479, DF: 10)

Is this influence of the unused groups on the p-value calculation intended? And if so, what's the rationale behind this?

I've created a minimal example for the mentioned protein Q9Z1D1:

library(tidyverse) # tidyverse      * 2.0.0   2023-02-22 [1] CRAN (R 4.2.1)
library(MSstats) #  MSstats        * 4.9.5   2023-07-14 [1] Github (Vitek-Lab/MSstats@d936898)

#load full dataProcess dataframe
load("/home/schori0001/ProjectSQ/PScheiffele/RaulOrtiz_521/20230530-105637_ro-007/SpectroNaut/20230628_103337_P521_PSchei_ro-007_mouse4Prot_SN18_20230628/230721_MSstats_all/Rdata/quantdata.rda")

#filter out a single protein as minimal example
QuantData$FeatureLevelData <- QuantData$FeatureLevelData %>% filter(grepl("Q9Z1D1", PROTEIN))
QuantData$ProteinLevelData <- QuantData$ProteinLevelData %>% filter(grepl("Q9Z1D1", Protein))

#export .rda file as minimal example
save(QuantData, file = "/home/schori0001/ProjectSQ/PScheiffele/RaulOrtiz_521/20230530-105637_ro-007/SpectroNaut/20230628_103337_P521_PSchei_ro-007_mouse4Prot_SN18_20230628/230721_MSstats_all/Rdata/quantdata_Q9Z1D1.rda")

#our target comparison is group A vs B. But groups C and E have stronger variability and also different LogIntensities (Group C)
ggplot(QuantData$ProteinLevelData, aes(GROUP, LogIntensities)) + geom_boxplot() + geom_point()

###########

#run groupsComparison on only 2 groups (A vs B) of this dataset, but keep other Groups in DF:
comparison <- as.data.frame(MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", unique(QuantData$ProteinLevelData$GROUP)))[1,]
# A  B C D E
# A vs B 1 -1 0 0 0
pw_comparison_unfiltered <- groupComparison(comparison, QuantData)

pw_comparison_unfiltered$ComparisonResult %>% filter(!is.na(log2FC))
Protein  Label    log2FC        SE   Tvalue DF     pvalue adj.pvalue issue MissingPercentage ImputationPercentage
# 1        Q9Z1D1 A vs B 0.7391662 0.5006525 1.476406 25 0.15232117 0.15232117    NA              0.29           0.07916667
# 2 Q9Z1D1_TARGET A vs B 1.0493225 0.4613805 2.274310 24 0.03217461 0.06434923    NA              0.00           0.00000000

###########

#run groupComparsion on the only 2 groups left in this dataframe, after filtering out Groups C, D & E:
QuantData_filt <- c()
QuantData_filt$ProteinLevelData <- QuantData$ProteinLevelData %>% filter(GROUP %in% c("A", "B"))
pw_comparison_filtered <- groupComparison("pairwise", QuantData_filt)

pw_comparison_filtered$ComparisonResult %>% filter(!is.na(log2FC))
# Protein  Label    log2FC         SE   Tvalue DF       pvalue   adj.pvalue issue MissingPercentage ImputationPercentage
# 1        Q9Z1D1 A vs B 0.7391662 0.08348684 8.853685 10 4.793949e-06 9.587897e-06    NA              0.29           0.07916667
# 2 Q9Z1D1_TARGET A vs B 1.0493225 0.22541154 4.655141 10 9.009575e-04 9.009575e-04    NA              0.00           0.00000000    

Thank you very much for looking into this and for the clarification!

Best,
Christian

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: number of groups in dataframe influence p-value of pairwise comparison
parts:
Hi Christian,

Yes this is a correct (and intended) behavior. MSstats makes the assumption that the variance of protein abundance is approximately same in all the groups. In some sense, using more groups with similar variances is a proxy for using more replicates. Therefore, even if you only compare two groups, MSstats uses all the groups to estimate the variation at the model fitting stage. This results in better numerical stability, more degrees of freedom, and better sensitivity of each pairwise comparison. 

There can of course be experiments where the assumption of similar variance between all the conditions is not verified. In these cases it is best to restrict the modeling to the groups being compared only. But in our experience, the default MSstats case is quite common. 

I hope that this helps at least somewhat. Thank you for using MSstats.
Olga
